incidents.baseline_or_control: The reporter says the Triton FP8 GEMM produced correct numerical output, and a llama.cpp Q5_K_M GGUF checkpoint produced coherent output at 20.6 tok/s.
incidents.discriminating_test: Run the same FP8_BLOCK checkpoint and prompts with dynamic per-token activation quantization enabled versus skipped; recovery only when skipped isolates runtime scale handling from checkpoint damage.
incidents.mechanism: The report's instrumentation identifies absorbed activation scales being applied again by dynamic per-token activation quantization, inflating hidden states until logits saturate. It separately reports that the SM 12.0 Triton fallback is numerically correct.
incidents.observed_failure: The checkpoint loads and tokenizes, but prompts produce indefinite repetitions such as " a a a a"; traced hidden-state norms inflate and the winning logit becomes pinned at 23.625.
incidents.optimization: FP8_BLOCK checkpoint produced by llm-compressor; W8A8 block FP8 with static weight scales and absorbed activation scales
incidents.rationale: Double-applied activation scales are confirmed; one runtime toggle cleanly tests the mechanism.

incidents.baseline_or_control: FP8 checkpoints of the same model are unaffected. Captured-call ablations report fp32 routing bias produces NaNs, while casting the same values to bf16, adding 10 to logits, or de-duplicating the bias produces clean output. A pre-regression build was healthy, and half-revert bisection identified d8462f49619.
incidents.discriminating_test: Replay the captured routing call with identical logits and weights, changing only routing_bias from fp32 to bf16; NaN only with fp32 localizes the failure to runtime routing rather than FP4 expert-weight damage.
incidents.mechanism: Removal of the bf16 correction-bias branch leaves an fp32 routing bias on the FP4 path. For very negative router logits, sigmoid contributions vanish at the fp32 bias scale; duplicated bias values then create exact ties across the top-8 boundary, and flashinfer routingCustom emits NaN expert weights that propagate to all logits. Standalone replay also shows the kernel's underlying defect is NaN-producing tie handling, not dtype alone.
missing_information: Whether closure corresponds to a merged fix
incidents.observed_failure: Beyond roughly 6.5k tokens for triggering content, output becomes repeated '!' characters; requested token logprobs are null because logits become all-NaN. Short requests are reported as healthy.
incidents.optimization: ModelOpt FP4 with flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner; FP8 KV cache
incidents.rationale: Captured-call dtype ablations isolate a NaN-producing routing tie at a sharp context threshold.
incidents.runtime_hardware: SGLang v0.5.15 or a build containing d8462f49619; 4× NVIDIA B300 / SM103, TP=4; standalone failing-kernel replay on 1 GPU
incidents.title: [Bug] GLM-5.2-NVFP4 + flashinfer_trtllm: long-context outputs collapse to '!!!!' (NaN logits) — fp32 correction_bias regression from #29783

incidents.baseline_or_control: The same prompts are clean with FP8 query and speculation on, with BF16 query and speculation off, and in no-window or q_len≤4 kernel controls; corruption occurs in both CUDA-graph and eager modes.

incidents.mechanism: The reporter attributes the main corruption to FlashInfer's trtllm-gen spec-as-decode kernel miscomputing BF16-Q/FP8-KV sliding-window attention at certain sequence-length/page alignments. Independently, vLLM is reported to apply q_scale when Q remains BF16 and to reapply k/v scales after KV dequantization.
incidents.observed_failure: After sequence length passes the 1024-token sliding window, deterministic generations show sporadic wrong tokens and short repetition loops; deeper speculation produces runaway repetition. The reporter also identifies double or unnecessary application of q/k/v scales for calibrated checkpoints.
incidents.optimization: NVFP4 model; FP8 E4M3 KV cache; BF16 query via disable_flashinfer_q_quantization; MTP speculative decoding
incidents.rationale: The failure appears only after the sliding-window boundary and has clean query-precision/speculation controls.

incidents.baseline_or_control: Forced cublas or cudnn-only backends reportedly avoid the crash, while backend="auto" triggers it.
incidents.discriminating_test: Capture a CUDA graph that references the shared workspace, grow that workspace through _get_cache_buf or _cudnn_gemm_fp8, and replay; compare with an otherwise identical run where the old tensor is retained.
incidents.mechanism: Instrumentation showed workspace.resize_ or cache replacement freeing the old allocation while captured graph nodes retained its address; a later oversized cuDNN plan grew the shared buffer mid-capture sequence, leaving earlier graphs with dangling pointers.
incidents.observed_failure: At replay, the stale workspace pointer causes either an Xid 31 GPU MMU fault and unspecified launch failure or silent memory corruption; the production configuration crashed 5/5 times.
incidents.optimization: FP8 per-tensor checkpoint; bmm_fp8 backend="auto"; FULL+PIECEWISE CUDA graphs; TP8
incidents.rationale: A confirmed captured-graph dangling pointer can produce either Xid failure or silent replay corruption.
